title: Overhead Press
summary: Standing barbell overhead press: front delts 1, triceps 0.6, side delts 0.5. The heaviest way to train overhead pressing.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights).

muscles.why: The front delts raise the arm overhead.
The triceps lock out the elbow; short heads 0.6, long head 0.3.
Upper traps rotate the shoulder blades up at the top.
The trunk braces to stay upright; below the counting floor (0.2).
The obliques help brace; below the counting floor (0.15).

setup.text: Bar in a rack at upper-chest height.
Grip just outside the shoulders; elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Feet hip width, glutes and abs tight.

form_cues.cue: Squeeze glutes and brace your abs
form_cues.why: Moving the head back lets the bar travel in a straight line.

form_cues.cue: Move your head back as the bar passes your face
form_cues.why: Bar over mid-foot at the top is balanced.

form_cues.cue: Finish with the bar over mid-foot
form_cues.why: Squeezing the glutes stops the lower back arching.

form_cues.cue: Squeeze your glutes so you don't lean back into the lift.
form_cues.why: Standing presses gave higher delt EMG but a lower 1RM than seated presses.
Finishes with the bar over the shoulders and mid-foot.

bias_tweaks.effect: More load, a little less delt EMG, less balance demand.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Leaning back hard and turning it into an incline press.
mistakes.fix: Lighten the load until you can press without leaning back.

mistakes.text: Pressing the bar forward around the face.
mistakes.fix: Move the head, not the bar.

misconceptions.myth: Overhead pressing builds the side delts as well as raises.
misconceptions.reality: Pressing works the front delts most; side delts are rated 0.5.

misconceptions.myth: Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: Ramp up before your first working set. For primary lifts the app suggests 50% x 8, 70% x 4 and 85% x 2 when the first working load is 60 kg or more, and 50% x 8 then 75% x 3 below that.
lower_risk.note: High-load warm-ups improved strength performance in a systematic review; the percentages are coaching convention.

lower_risk.text: Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 6-10 rep range. Stop the set before you lean back to finish reps.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Machine path: low fatigue, easy to push close to failure.
Lying on a bench: no standing balance; more chest.

notes: Overhead press findings are EMG and 1RM only.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
